stem:
The elements sodium to sulfur react with chlorine. The melting points of some of the chlorides formed are shown.

| chloride | $\text{NaCl}$ | $\text{MgCl}_2$ | $\text{AlCl}_3$ | $\text{SiCl}_4$ | $\text{PCl}_3$ | $\text{SCl}_2$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| melting point/$\text{K}$ | 1074 | 987 | 463 | 203 | 161 | 195 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Predict the shapes of $\text{AlCl}_3$ and $\text{PCl}_3$.

Draw diagrams to show the shapes, name the shapes and state the bond angles.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why the melting point of $\text{SiCl}_4$ is much lower than that of $\text{NaCl}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the melting point of $\text{SiCl}_4$ is higher than that of $\text{PCl}_3$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Draw the 'dot-and-cross' diagram of a molecule of $\text{SiCl}_4$.
Show outer electrons only.
